title: Windowed KV spillover controller and stabilized GPU paging behavior for continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We observe recurring latency spikes and OOMs under sustained continuous-batching workloads when the KV cache resident set oscillates. Existing eviction is reactive and per-slice, causing frequent GPU-to-host swap churn and tail latency regressions. This ticket implements a windowed spillover controller that coordinates slab residency across batching boundaries to stabilize GPU paging behavior and reduce swap amplification.

Goals:
- Reduce swap-induced tail latency by creating cooperative residency windows across batches.
- Limit swap amplification by aggregating demotions/promotions and aligning them with batching epochs.
- Add heuristics to pin hot prefixes for short windows and to gracefully demote cold slices with hysteresis.
- Provide observability and fallbacks (soft backpressure, model variant fallback) when pressure exceeds thresholds.

Scope: Host-side controller and small runtime hooks (lease tokens & sync points). No model format changes. Includes telemetry, integration tests, and a canary rollout to a subset of Dedicated nodes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests showing >=3x reduction in GPU-host swap ops for steady-state LLM generation on the benchmark harness compared to baseline.
95th token latency improvement of at least 20% on continuous-batching scenarios that previously triggered thrashing.
No functional regressions: cached outputs identical to baseline for pinned/resident ranges.
Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.kv.windowed_spillover_enabled and can be toggled at runtime.
Dashboards: memory-pressure-slope, spillops-per-epoch, window-residency-occupancy added to console and retained for 30d.
Safety: fallback policy to model-variant or rate-limited backpressure when memory-pressure-slope reaches emergency threshold.
decision_log: 2026-01-18: Chose host-side spillover controller over fully in-GPU solution to avoid cross-vendor kernel work and to leverage existing async IO stack. - Maya C., Nikhil P.

2026-01-21: Use epoch-aligned demote/promote batches (window size default=200ms) to amortize swap ops across many requests. Hysteresis factor set to 1.5x occupancy delta to avoid flip-flop. - Performance/Infra sync

2026-01-25: Opted for cooperative lease tokens that live for the window duration. This keeps resident sets stable during the batching epoch. Leases are reconcilable at the next epoch boundary. - Luca R., SRE

2026-01-20 - Luca Romano: Implemented host spillover controller prototype and added lease-token API hook in runtime. Basic end-to-end smoke tested on dev-gpu-3.

2026-01-28 - Priya S.: Benchmarked prototype under 512-token avg sequences; observed 2.1x reduction in swap ops but tail latency unchanged due to aggressive demote timing. Tuned window to 300ms for smoother behavior.

implementation_notes: Controller responsibilities: observe recent resident-set deltas, compute memory-pressure-slope metric, schedule demote/promote ops aligned to epoch windows, and emit metrics (spillops, window_miss_rate, memory_pressure_slope).

Lease tokens: ephemeral strings with (slice_id, epoch_id, pin_policy). Tokens are reconciled at epoch boundary; runtime honors tokens and refuses demote of pinned slices until next epoch except under emergency OOM path.

Demote sequence: aggregate cold slices across tenants into an async batch write to host NVMe; coalesce IOs to reduce overhead. Promote sequence: prefetch KV slabs back into GPU during warmup gaps or prefetched into staging host buffers if bandwidth-limited.
Hysteresis/Grace periods: two levels - window-level (200-500ms) and emergency-level (sustained pressure > 3s triggers immediate eviction and model fallback).

Backpressure: Controller exposes a soft-backpressure API (http 429 with Retry-After heuristics) for the front-end scheduler when memory_pressure_slope is high; also supports routing to lower-capacity model variant.
Telemetry: add spillops_total, spillops_epoch_count, epoch_window_ms, resident_occupancy_pct, memory_pressure_slope, lease_pin_conflicts.
benchmarks: Baseline: continuous-batching harness with BERT-like prefix distribution - swap ops 8400/min, 95th token latency 240ms.
Prototype (window=200ms): swap ops 3400/min, 95th token latency 210ms (no model fallback).
Tuned (window=300ms + coalesced IO): swap ops 2400/min, 95th token latency 185ms, observed 30% reduction in tail compared to baseline.
Emergency stress (synthetic churn): windowed controller prevented OOM in 9/10 runs; baseline failed 6/10.
risks: Increased latency for occasional requests if controller pins large hot prefixes and prevents eviction long enough to cause temporary overcommit.
Complexity surge: lease reconciliation adds state that must be durable across control-plane reboots for Private deployments; need migration plan.
Edge-case races: simultaneous lease expiry + batch commit can cause double-write to host if not soft-locked. Mitigated by a cheap compare-and-swap in host queue.
